details.formulaDescription: heatScore = temperatureC + 0.04 × relativeHumidityPercent, rounded to one decimal. Bands: below 10 cool, 10 to below 18 moderate, 18 to below 24 hot, 24 to below 30 very hot, 30 or above extreme. Each band maps to an experience-based slowdown range: cool 0-2%, moderate 2-5%, hot 5-8%, very hot 7-10%, extreme 10-12%. adjustedPaceLowSeconds = round(baselinePaceSecondsPerKm × (1 + lowPercent / 100)) and adjustedPaceHighSeconds = round(baselinePaceSecondsPerKm × (1 + highPercent / 100)). Duration is recorded as exposure context and does not change the percentages.
assumptions: The heat score is a simple monotonic weighted sum of temperature and humidity, not an official heat-index formula.
The slowdown percentages are an experience-based range, not an official conversion or a prediction of individual performance.
Baseline pace is a flat, mild-weather aerobic pace; a hilly or altitude course needs separate adjustment.
Relative humidity is the value at the planned running time and is assumed constant for the session.
Duration is used as exposure context only; longer sessions should use the upper end of the range and extra caution.
The tool does not provide medical advice; heat-illness symptoms require stopping and, for emergencies, calling emergency services.
details.rounding: Heat score to one decimal place; adjusted pace low and high to the nearest whole second per kilometre; percentages are integers; the note is text and is not rounded.
